rules: Total population is split between assigned professions and unemployed citizens.
Each citizen assigned to a profession contributes production, on top of building bonuses.

Recruiting N warriors immediately reduces total population by N, drawn only from unemployed citizens — you can recruit at most as many warriors as you currently have unemployed (reassign workers to unemployed first if you need more; see reassignment). This loss is not permanent: like any other population loss, it recovers over subsequent turns through normal growth (see growth) once food income is positive again.
Reassigning citizens between professions costs 1 AP per batch of reassignments in a turn.
Population never goes below 1 in the player's capital while the game is active.

professions.produces: stone, copper, iron, or gold (assigned at placement)

professions.effect: No production. Large numbers of unemployed citizens slowly reduce happiness.

growth.rule: Population grows when food income exceeds food consumption.
growth.growth_chance_formula: min(food_surplus / 20, 0.5) chance per turn to add 1 new citizen
growth.new_citizen_assignment: New citizens are added as unemployed by default; the player assigns them manually.

reassignment.rule: The player may move any number of citizens between professions in a single reassignment action.

happiness_interaction.rule: Happiness below 50% reduces all production by a percentage; happiness below 25% risks unrest events.
happiness_interaction.unemployment_penalty: Every 5 unemployed citizens above a small free buffer reduces happiness by 1%.
